meta.title: Three-Dimensional Bioprinting of Astrocytes and Endothelial Cells to Direct Retinal Axon Growth and Vascularization.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Optic nerve head astrocytes and endothelial cells were printed at the centre of retinal ganglion cell scaffolds to recreate how the retinal nerve fibre layer develops. Developing astrocytes increased RGC neurite polarization by 43%.

formulations.review_notes: No viability percentage or print pressure in the text.
formulations.name: Matrigel (astrocyte core)
formulations.composition_detail: undiluted Matrigel (also screened: 4 mg/mL collagen-1, 1% alginate, 1% alginate-RGD)
formulations.key_outcome: Astrocytes from the developing optic nerve head increased retinal ganglion cell neurite alignment by 43%.

evidence.quote: printed using a 22 g needle in four previously published bioinks: undiluted matrigel, 4 mg/mL collagen-1, 1% alginate, and 1% alginate-modified with RGD cell binding domain peptides
Cells were resuspended in matrigel at 4°C at a concentration of 1–1.5 × 106 cells/mL
Bioprinting was conducted using an extrusion-based Allevi 3 bioprinter (3D systems).
